s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of gross hematuria and flank pain with a palpable mass and systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Large right renal mass with hemorrhage and invasion of the collecting system, renal vein, and inferior vena cava
key_facts: 2-week history of gross hematuria
Right lower-quadrant pain
Low-grade fever
No relief from empirical treatment for urinary tract infection
Tenderness to palpation in the right upper and suprapubic regions
Urinalysis showed 2+ blood but no evidence of infection
Urine β-hCG was negative
Normal white-cell count
Mild anemia with hemoglobin of 11.2 g/dL and hematocrit of 33.2 %
Normal renal and hepatic function tests
Large, heterogeneously attenuating right renal mass on noncontrast abdominopelvic CT scan
Invasion of the collecting system, right renal vein, and inferior vena cava on contrast-enhanced CT
Multiple small bilateral pulmonary nodules on staging chest CT

shortlist.label: Renal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large, heterogeneously attenuating right renal mass with invasion of the collecting system, right renal vein, and inferior vena cava, and multiple small bilateral pulmonary nodules

shortlist.label: Angiomyolipoma with hemorrhage
shortlist.why_kept: Heterogeneously attenuating mass with foci of hyperattenuation suggesting hemorrhage, although less likely given systemic symptoms and pulmonary nodules

shortlist.label: Renal sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive features of the mass, including invasion of the collecting system, right renal vein, and inferior vena cava, and presence of systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Collecting duct carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Invasion of the collecting system and aggressive features of the mass, although less common than renal cell carcinoma

shortlist.label: Papillary renal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a large, heterogeneously attenuating renal mass with systemic symptoms and pulmonary nodules, consistent with metastatic disease

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with gross hematuria, flank pain, and a large, heterogeneously attenuating renal mass with invasion of the collecting system, renal vein, and inferior vena cava, along with multiple small bilateral pulmonary nodules, is most consistent with renal cell carcinoma, which is known for its potential to cause hematuria, pain, and metastasis.

rejected.label: Angiomyolipoma with hemorrhage
rejected.why: While angiomyolipoma can cause hemorrhage, it is typically benign and less likely to cause systemic symptoms or metastasis.

rejected.label: Renal sarcoma
rejected.why: Renal sarcoma is rare and would not typically present with the combination of hematuria, flank pain, and a large renal mass with vascular invasion.

rejected.label: Collecting duct carcinoma
rejected.why: Collecting duct carcinoma is a rare subtype of renal cell carcinoma, but the patient's presentation and imaging findings are more consistent with a more common type of renal cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Papillary renal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: While papillary renal cell carcinoma is a subtype of renal cell carcinoma, the patient's presentation and imaging findings do not specifically suggest this subtype over the more general diagnosis of renal cell carcinoma.
